level1.text: A capacitor is connected to a voltage of $12\,\text{V}$, and a charge of $4.8\,\mu\text{C}$ moves to its plates. What is the capacitance of the capacitor? Give the answer in microfarads.

The capacitance of an electrolytic capacitor is $470\,\mu\text{F}$, and it is charged with a $9.0\,\text{V}$ battery. How large is the charge of the capacitor after charging? Give the answer in millicoulombs.

The power supply of a speaker amplifier has a capacitor with a capacitance of $2200\,\mu\text{F}$ and a voltage of $16\,\text{V}$. How much energy is stored in the capacitor? Give the answer in joules.

The area of the plates of a parallel-plate capacitor is $0.025\,\text{m}^2$, and there is a layer of air $1.0\,\text{mm}$ thick between the plates. What is the capacitance of the capacitor? Give the answer in picofarads.

The graph shows the voltage of a capacitor as a function of its charge during charging. How much energy is stored in the capacitor when its voltage is $12\,\text{V}$? Read the necessary values from the graph. Give the answer in microjoules.
A capacitor is first charged to a voltage of $5.0\,\text{V}$ and then to $10\,\text{V}$. What happens to the capacitance of the capacitor?
level1.answer: It stays the same, because the capacitance is determined by the construction of the capacitor.

choices.text: It doubles, because the charge grows in the same proportion as the voltage.
choices.feedback: The charge does grow in the same proportion as the voltage, but the capacitance is their ratio $\tfrac{Q}{U}$, so it does not change.

choices.text: It decreases, because a higher voltage strains the plates and weakens the ability to store charge.
choices.feedback: The capacitance does not weaken as the voltage grows. It depends only on the construction; the strain matters only when the field approaches the dielectric strength of the dielectric.

choices.text: It becomes four times as large, because the energy of the capacitor depends on the square of the voltage.
choices.feedback: The energy $W = \tfrac{1}{2} C U^2$ becomes four times as large when the voltage doubles, but that is exactly why $C$ is a constant in the formula. The capacitance itself does not change.

choices.text: It stays the same, because the capacitance is determined by the construction of the capacitor.
choices.feedback: Correct: the capacitance $C = \tfrac{Q}{U}$ depends on the area of the plates, their distance and the dielectric. When the voltage doubles, the charge doubles too, and the ratio stays the same.

level1.text: The source is disconnected from a charged parallel-plate capacitor with air between the plates. After that a plate of dielectric that fills the whole space is pushed between the plates. What happens to the voltage of the capacitor?
level1.answer: It decreases, because the charge stays the same and the capacitance increases.

choices.text: It increases, because the capacitance increases and the charge stays the same.
choices.feedback: The charge does stay the same, but the voltage is $U = \tfrac{Q}{C}$. When $C$ increases and $Q$ stays the same, the voltage decreases and does not increase.

choices.text: It stays the same, because the voltage is determined by the source with which the capacitor was charged.
choices.feedback: The source has been disconnected, so it no longer keeps the voltage constant. The voltage follows from the charge and the capacitance, and the capacitance changed.

choices.text: It decreases, because the charge stays the same and the capacitance increases.
choices.feedback: Correct: the charge of a disconnected capacitor cannot change, and the dielectric increases the capacitance. Since $U = \tfrac{Q}{C}$, the voltage decreases.

choices.text: It decreases, because the dielectric lets charge pass from one plate to the other.
choices.feedback: The dielectric does not conduct charge: its task is not to conduct. The charge of a disconnected capacitor stays the same, and the voltage decreases because the capacitance increases.

level1.text: The capacitance of a capacitor in the power supply of a computer is $1000\,\mu\text{F}$. Its voltage rises from $6.0\,\text{V}$ to $18\,\text{V}$. By how much does the energy of the capacitor increase? Give the answer in millijoules.
A capacitor with a capacitance of $100\,\mu\text{F}$ is charged through a resistor with a $12\,\text{V}$ battery until the current stops flowing. Decide which statements are true and which are false.

statements.text: The charges of the plates are $+1.2\,\text{mC}$ and $-1.2\,\text{mC}$, so the total charge of the capacitor is zero.
statements.feedback: Correct: $Q = CU$, that is, $Q = 100\,\mu\text{F} \cdot 12\,\text{V} = 1.2\,\text{mC}$. The battery only moves charge from one plate to the other, so the charges of the plates are equal and opposite.

statements.text: After charging has ended, current passes through the insulator between the plates in the same way as in conductors.
statements.feedback: Wrong: this is the idea that current passes through a capacitor like through a conductor. The insulator does not conduct electricity, so charge does not pass through it, and current passes in the conductors only while the charge of the plates changes. At the end of charging the current is zero.

statements.text: If the capacitor were charged to a voltage of $24\,\text{V}$, its capacitance would be twice as large.
statements.feedback: Wrong: this assumes that capacitance grows with voltage. Double the voltage brings double the charge, so the ratio $C = \tfrac{Q}{U}$ stays at $100\,\mu\text{F}$.

statements.text: Energy of $14.4\,\text{mJ}$ has been stored in the capacitor.
statements.feedback: Wrong: $14.4\,\text{mJ}$ is the energy given by the battery, $QU$, that is, $1.2\,\text{mC} \cdot 12\,\text{V}$. The charge moves on average across a voltage of $\tfrac{U}{2}$, so the energy stored in the capacitor is $\tfrac{1}{2} QU = 7.2\,\text{mJ}$.

statements.text: If the capacitor were charged to a voltage of $24\,\text{V}$, its energy would be four times as large.
statements.feedback: Correct: the energy $W = \tfrac{1}{2} C U^2$ depends on the square of the voltage. When $C$ stays the same and the voltage doubles, the energy grows $2^2 = 4$-fold, to $28.8\,\text{mJ}$.

level2.text: Between the plates of a capacitor there is a layer of paper $0.020\,\text{mm}$ thick, whose dielectric strength is $16\,\text{MV/m}$. What is the greatest voltage that can be connected to the capacitor without a breakdown?

The area of the plates of a parallel-plate capacitor is $100\,\text{cm}^2$, and between them there is a layer of dielectric $0.10\,\text{mm}$ thick. The capacitance of the capacitor is measured to be $3.3\,\text{nF}$. What is the relative permittivity of the dielectric?

Energy of $200\,\text{J}$ is stored in the capacitor of a defibrillator before the shock, when its voltage is $2.0\,\text{kV}$. What is the capacitance of the capacitor? Give the answer in microfarads.

The capacitance of a supercapacitor is $10\,\text{F}$, and it has been charged to its maximum allowed voltage of $2.7\,\text{V}$. It powers an LED lamp whose power is $0.50\,\text{W}$. Assume that the power stays constant and that all the energy of the capacitor can be used. How long does the lamp stay lit? Give the answer in seconds.

The capacitance of a capacitor is studied by charging it to different voltages. The charge $Q$ in the table has been calculated from the measured charging current (example data).

a) Draw the $(U, Q)$ graph of the points, fit a straight line through the origin to the points, and determine the capacitance from the slope of the line.

b) Calculate the energy stored in the capacitor at the voltage $12\,\text{V}$. Give the answer in millijoules.

The answer box takes the result of part b).

level2.text: A capacitor is charged through a resistor with a $9.0\,\text{V}$ battery, and its voltage is measured at intervals of one second (example data). Study the table or draw a graph of the points. During which time interval is the charging current the greatest?
level2.answer: During the interval $0\text{–}1\,\text{s}$, because the voltage then grows the fastest.

choices.text: During the interval $1\text{–}2\,\text{s}$, because the voltage is then about half of the voltage of the source.
choices.feedback: The size of the voltage does not tell the current, but its rate of change does. In this interval the voltage grows only $2.0\,\text{V}$, whereas at the start it grew $3.5\,\text{V}$ in one second.

choices.text: During the interval $4\text{–}5\,\text{s}$, because the current grows when more charge has accumulated in the capacitor.
choices.feedback: The accumulated charge decreases the current: the voltage between the plates opposes the source, and charging slows down. In this interval the voltage grows only $0.5\,\text{V}$.

choices.text: During the interval $0\text{–}1\,\text{s}$, because the voltage then grows the fastest.
choices.feedback: Correct: the current is the rate of change of the charge, and since $Q = CU$, it is directly proportional to the rate at which the voltage grows. The graph is steepest at the start, when the current is the greatest.

choices.text: During the interval $5\text{–}6\,\text{s}$, because the voltage is then at its greatest and the charge is at its greatest.
choices.feedback: A large voltage means a large charge, not a large current. The current is the rate of change of the charge, and in this interval the voltage grows the slowest, only $0.3\,\text{V}$.

level2.text:
A student solves a problem: “The capacitance of a capacitor is $220\,\mu\text{F}$, and it is charged with a voltage source of $24\,\text{V}$. The source moves to the capacitor a charge $Q = CU = 5.28\,\text{mC}$ and gives an energy $QU = 127\,\text{mJ}$. All this energy is stored in the capacitor, so $W = 127\,\text{mJ}$.”

a) What is the error in the student’s reasoning? Justify briefly.

b) Calculate correctly the energy stored in the capacitor in millijoules.

The answer box takes the result of part b).

level3.text: A parallel-plate capacitor with air between the plates and a capacitance of $120\,\text{pF}$ is charged to a voltage of $500\,\text{V}$, and the source is disconnected. Then the plates are pulled twice as far apart. By how much does the energy of the capacitor increase? Give the answer in microjoules.

A capacitor with air between the plates and a capacitance of $220\,\text{pF}$ is connected to a voltage source of $1.5\,\text{kV}$. The space between the plates is filled with a glass plate whose relative permittivity is $5.6$, and the source stays connected all the time. How much additional charge moves from the source to the capacitor? Give the answer in microcoulombs.

You are designing a parallel-plate capacitor with a capacitance of $1.0\,\text{nF}$ that withstands a voltage of $6.0\,\text{kV}$. The dielectric is polystyrene, whose relative permittivity is $2.6$ and dielectric strength $24\,\text{MV/m}$. To be safe, the field may be at most half of the dielectric strength. How large must the area of the plates be? Give the answer in square centimetres.

The capacitor of a defibrillator is charged with a constant current of $15\,\text{mA}$. The table gives the voltage of the capacitor during charging (example data). The shock is given when the voltage is $1.8\,\text{kV}$, and the capacitor discharges through the patient in $5.0\,\text{ms}$.

With a constant current the charge grows steadily, $Q = It$, so the voltage is directly proportional to time.

a) Determine the capacitance using the slope of the straight line through the origin that is fitted to the points of the table.

b) Calculate the average power released in the shock in kilowatts.

c) How long does charging to $1.8\,\text{kV}$ take? Why must the capacitor of the device not be touched even when the device has been unplugged?

The answer box takes the result of part b). Justify part c) in writing.

level3.text:
Two parallel-plate capacitors are made of similar plates: the area of a plate is $100\,\text{cm}^2$ and the thickness of the dielectric layer is $0.050\,\text{mm}$. In one the dielectric is Teflon and in the other glass (table). To be safe, the field may be at most half of the dielectric strength in both. Use the electric constant $\varepsilon_0 = 8.854 \cdot 10^{-12}\,\text{F/m}$.

a) Calculate the greatest allowed voltage and the capacitance of each capacitor.

b) Calculate the energy of each capacitor at this voltage. How many times as large is the energy of the Teflon capacitor as that of the glass capacitor?

c) The relative permittivity of glass is greater than that of Teflon, but Teflon stores more energy. Explain why.

The answer box takes the ratio of the energies of part b). Justify part c) in writing.
